ES.label: S&P 500 Fut
ES.source: E-mini S&P 500 continuous, 7697.75 quoted 11:21:33 UTC. Prior reference 7708.75, the close of the 16:45 UTC 15-minute bar on 9/07 - the last bar before the CME Labor Day halt, on 1458 contracts, so a real print rather than a stub. Post-reopen overnight range 7687.75 to 7725.75, re-derived from the same bar series. The index is therefore a fifth of a percent lower than where the abbreviated holiday session left it, having traded a 38-point band overnight. BASE SELECTION, disclosed in full because it is contestable. CME did not derive or disseminate settlement prices for any CME, CBOT, NYMEX or COMEX product on Monday 9/7 - the exchange's own Labor Day settlement notice says so, and its clearing advisory carries prices forward from the prior day. So there is NO official Monday settlement to measure against. Three candidate bases existed and all three were computed. (1) The vendor's daily 9/07 aggregate. (2) The vendor's previousClose field. (3) The last print before the exchange's documented 1:00 PM ET holiday halt, re-derived this run from 15-minute bars. Basis 3 is shipped: the bar series shows a clean five-hour gap from 16:45/17:00 UTC to 22:00 UTC, and 22:00 UTC is 6:00 PM ET, which is exactly the 17:00 CT reopen published in CME's holiday calendar. The gap boundary derived independently from price data matches the exchange document to the minute, which is what makes basis 3 defensible and the other two arbitrary. The vendor's previousClose for NQ was NOT rolled past Friday at all and would have shown a -0.02% move; the daily aggregate would have shown -0.61%. The escalation threshold for this run is a 2% overnight futures move and it is NOT tripped under any of the three bases - worst case across all of them is 0.563%. That robustness is the reason the ambiguity did not need to be resolved before shipping. CASH CONTEXT: NOT ATH: the S&P 500 cash index closed Friday at 7718.60, -1.031% below its record close of 7798.99 set 8/13/26 and -1.255% below the 7816.70 peak intraday high from that session. This is context for the futures tile above, not a live level - SPX cash has not printed since Friday. The e-mini is the only S&P instrument on today's board carrying a Tuesday timestamp.

WTI.label: WTI Crude
WTI.source: CLUSD front-month futures, 93.98 against Monday's 92.70 electronic close. Up a fourth consecutive session and the strongest tile on the board in percentage terms among instruments that actually traded. Friday's US settlement - the last clean one - was 91.48, so crude is 2.73% above the last settled American print. The vendor's previousClose rolled correctly here, which it did not for Brent. BASE RE-DERIVED, NOT TAKEN FROM THE VENDOR. This run found that the quote vendor's previousClose field rolls per-instrument and inconsistently through a holiday session: four of nine instruments checked had NOT rolled past Friday, and on the dollar index the stale base produced an outright SIGN FLIP. Every base on this board was therefore re-derived from daily OHLCV bars for the specific date, and the staleness test used was whether the vendor's base sat nearer Friday's close than Monday's - not a bare numeric tolerance, which produced a false positive on AUD/JPY where a 5-pip difference is just rounding.

VIX.label: VIX
VIX.source: Cboe VIX, FRIDAY's 14.53 settle against Thursday's 14.32. THIS TILE REJECTS TWO NEWER INPUTS AND THE REJECTION IS THE POINT. The data vendor serves an I:VIX bar for 9/07 - a day the US cash market was closed and Cboe does not compute the index - and that bar has now MUTATED between fetches on three separate occasions across three runs: read as close 15.14 with a 15.16 high, then 15.17, and this run as open 15.02, high 15.32, low 14.99, close 15.30. A settled closing value does not move three times, so the bar is not a settle. Run #175 rejected it on two fetches; the third mutation retroactively vindicates that call. The vendor also serves a 9/08 bar which is a live pre-open partial and is likewise mutating. REJECTED INPUT: 15.17, and the 15.30 that replaced it. The decisive corroborating argument is a missing sibling - the same vendor serves NO 9/07 or 9/08 bar for I:SPX, I:NDX, I:SOX, I:DJI or VXN. A feed that had genuinely computed holiday volatility would not have computed it for exactly one index. INDICATIVE ONLY, never on the tile: VIX futures and the pre-open implied level sit near 15.8, roughly 9% above Friday's settle, against S&P futures down 0.14% - a vol bid materially larger than the spot move justifies. That asymmetry is worth a desk's attention and is NOT a settled number. VXN's last real bar remains 20.04 from 9/04.
